note: كِتَاب (book) / كَتَبَ (he wrote) / مَكْتَبَة (library) — the same root printed three ways.
source: Standard MSA root morphology (Hans Wehr root ك ت ب); cross-checked against Wiktionary.

note: مَطْعَم (restaurant) / طَعَام (food) — a place-noun (مفعل pattern) built on the same root as the food it serves.
source: Standard MSA root morphology (Hans Wehr root ط ع م).

note: مِصْبَاح (lamp) / صَبَاح (morning) — the lamp is literally "the thing that shines/dawns".
source: Standard MSA root morphology (Hans Wehr root ص ب ح).

note: مَدْرَسَة (school) / دَرْس (lesson) — a place-noun (مفعل pattern) built on the same root as what happens there.
source: Standard MSA root morphology (Hans Wehr root د ر س).

note: جَدِيد (new) / جَدّ (grandfather) / جَدَّة (grandmother) — a genuinely non-obvious pairing ("grandparent" and "new" don't look related in translation) that's a real, well-documented root family in Arabic, not a coincidence of spelling.
source: Standard MSA root morphology (Hans Wehr root ج د د); cross-checked against Wiktionary.

note: رَأَى (he saw) / مِرْآة (mirror) — an instrument-noun (مفعلة pattern), "the thing you see with".
source: Standard MSA root morphology (Hans Wehr root ر أ ي).

note: وَاحِد (one) / الْأَحَد (Sunday, literally "the first [day]") — five of the seven Arabic weekday names are built directly on the numbers 1-5.
source: Standard MSA root morphology; verified against Wiktionary and multiple weekday-etymology references (see content/m20.5-language-tools-review.md).

note: اِثْنَان (two) / الِاثْنَيْن (Monday) — same root, and visibly the same word with the definite article and dual ending.
source: Standard MSA root morphology; verified against Wiktionary and weekday-etymology references.
